requirements.requirement: Loading a Python file is blocking work that a stop interrupts
requirements.details: Starting the interpreter and running a file's top level happen on a blocking worker; a file looping at its top level ends at the deadline, which is the only failure reported.

documentation_updates.change: Check the macOS and Windows Python item.
Regenerated after this record added requirements.

validation_scope: Full GNU/musl debug/release suites: 2,098 tests each, and 2,107 with the python feature; strict Clippy for GNU, musl, the python feature, macOS, and Windows; helper checks, the editor packages, workflow lint, cargo publish --dry-run, and the public API; 9 Python catalogue faults, all caught; the whole suite with the python feature on Linux, macOS, and Windows in CI.
review_notes: macOS needed nothing beyond a Python: the one actions/setup-python installs links and embeds as on Linux.

A later Windows run failed the stop test's two-second bound at 4 s. The time measured included starting the interpreter, which a cold Windows host makes slow, and showed a real defect: loading a file, which starts the interpreter and runs the file's top level, ran on the async executor's own thread, where nothing could interrupt it and nothing else could run. Loading now runs as a blocking job under the same interruption as calls, a new test stops a file that loops while it loads, and the stop tests start the interpreter before timing.

Windows found the standard library from the interpreter's directory on PATH, and failed one test: an async statement run from the CLI raised 'set_wakeup_fd only works in main thread of the main interpreter'. The threading module takes whichever thread first imports it as the main thread, and the first import happened on a worker thread, so asyncio's proactor loop believed that thread was the main one and called signal.set_wakeup_fd, which CPython refused. The interpreter now imports threading on the thread that starts it.
limits: CI covers Python 3.12 on each platform; other 3.10+ versions are expected to work through the stable ABI but are not tested.

out=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pyplat-validation-",dir=root/"target"))
print(f"validation record: {out / 'summary.json'}",flush=True)
def measured():
 inputs=[p for d in ('src','tests','examples','editors','benches','usability') for p in (root/d).rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in p.parts and 'node_modules' not in p.parts and p.suffix != '.vsix']

 return {str(p.resolve().relative_to(root)):hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sorted(inputs)}

record['type_check_stubs']={'note':'No C cross compilers here: ring\'s build script gets stand-ins, so these checks type-check and lint without linking.','CC':'/bin/true','AR':Path(stub_ar).read_text()}
commands=[('gnu-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked']),('gnu-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release']),('musl-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked',*musl]),('musl-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release',*musl]),('clippy-gnu',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-musl',['cargo','clippy','--locked',*musl,'--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('format',['cargo','fmt','--all','--','--check']),('coverage-helper',['python3','tests/coverage_tools.py']),('mutation-helper',['python3','tests/mutation_tools.py']),('performance-helper',['python3','tests/performance_tools.py']),('vscode-package',['sh','-c','cd editors/vscode && npm run package']),('release-helper',['python3','tests/release_tools.py']),('workflow-lint',['/tmp/claude-1000/-home-dhilipsiva-projects-dhilipsiva-botwork/bf580eda-fba7-4d4c-8d68-f634c8c41a54/scratchpad/actionlint/actionlint','-shellcheck=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-dhilipsiva-projects-dhilipsiva-botwork/bf580eda-fba7-4d4c-8d68-f634c8c41a54/scratchpad/shellcheck-v0.11.0/shellcheck']),('crate-package',['cargo','publish','--locked','--dry-run']),('api-helper',['python3','tests/api_tools.py']),('public-api',['sh','-c','cargo +nightly-2026-08-14 rustdoc --lib --locked --target-dir target/api-check -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json && python3 scripts/public_api.py --leaks target/api-check/doc/botwork.json && python3 scripts/public_api.py target/api-check/doc/botwork.json | diff -u docs/public-api.txt -']),('python-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--no-fail-fast','--features','python']),('clippy-python',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--features','python','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-macos',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--target','aarch64-apple-darwin','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-windows',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--target','x86_64-pc-windows-msvc','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings'])]
previous=json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()) if len(sys.argv)>1 else None
if previous:
 assert previous['input_sha256']==record['input_sha256'], 'inputs changed since the resumed record'
 record['resumed_from']={'record':sys.argv[1],'sha256':hashlib.sha256(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'started':previous['started']}
 labels=[label for label,_ in commands]
 kept=[check for check in previous['checks'] if check['status']==0 and check['label'] in labels and [c for l,c in commands if l==check['label']][0]==check['command']]

  assert hashlib.sha256((root/check['log']).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==check['log_sha256']

 print('resumed', [check['label'] for check in kept], flush=True)
try:
 for label,command in commands:
  if any(check['label']==label for check in record['checks']):
   continue
  print('running '+label,flush=True)
  log=out/(label+'.log')
  with log.open('w') as stream:
   result=subprocess.run(command,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=2400,env=dict(os.environ,CARGO_BUILD_JOBS='4',CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_musl=musl_cc,BOTWORK_REQUIRE_EDITORS='all',**(stubs if label in ('clippy-macos','clippy-windows') else {})))
  content=log.read_text()
  rows=re.findall(r'test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;',content)

  record['checks'].append(check)

   print(content[-12000:],flush=True)

 record['inputs_unchanged']=measured()==record['input_sha256']

finally:

print('complete' if record['complete'] else 'INPUTS CHANGED', flush=True)

"""Record a CI run's jobs: conclusions, test totals, the Python job's tests
and the Python it linked, and the default build's refusal test."""
import hashlib, json, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
run, out = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
PYTHON = ["values_cross_into_python_and_back_unchanged", "values_without_an_exact_botwork_equivalent_are_refused", "exceptions_become_catchable_diagnostics_with_their_traceback", "module_globals_stay_within_one_run", "async_statements_run_their_coroutines", "a_stop_interrupts_python_and_leaves_the_interpreter_usable", "files_import_their_neighbours_while_loading", "loading_failures_are_import_errors", "the_cli_runs_python_statements", "a_stop_interrupts_a_file_while_it_loads"]
DEFAULT = ["python_modules_need_a_python_build"]
view = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["gh", "run", "view", run, "--json", "jobs,headSha,headBranch,conclusion"], text=True))
record = {"run": run, "url": f"https://github.com/dhilipsiva/botwork/actions/runs/{run}", "head_sha": view["headSha"], "branch": view["headBranch"], "conclusion": view["conclusion"], "jobs": {}}
for job in view["jobs"]:
    log = subprocess.check_output(["gh", "api", f"repos/dhilipsiva/botwork/actions/jobs/{job['databaseId']}/logs"], text=True)
    log = re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m", "", re.sub(r"^\S+Z ", "", log, flags=re.M))
    rows = re.findall(r"test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;", log)
    entry = {"conclusion": job["conclusion"], "log_sha256": hashlib.sha256(log.encode()).hexdigest()}
    if rows:
        entry["tests"] = dict(zip(("passed", "failed", "ignored"), [sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)]))
    entry["named"] = dict(re.findall(r"^test (?:\S+::)?(" + "|".join(PYTHON + DEFAULT) + r") \.\.\. (\w+)", log, re.M))
    if job["name"].startswith("Python adapter"):
        entry["python"] = re.findall(r"^Python 3\.\d+\.\d+$", log, re.M)
    record["jobs"][job["name"]] = entry
out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps({name: {k: v for k, v in job.items() if k != "log_sha256"} for name, job in record["jobs"].items()}, indent=1))
